title: Score each purchase without holding a session

blocks.text: Since the fraud-scoring service went live, terminals time out at lunchtime. The service needs up to two seconds for a score, and while one purchase waits for its score, the purchases queued behind it wait too.

`ScoreFraud`, in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/ScoreFraud.java`, asks the service about each purchase and leaves the score under `SCORE` in the Context. The participant after it, given in the tests, decides: 800 or more is declined with `59`. The service is the `Scorer` interface at the bottom of the file. It answers later, on a thread of its own, through the listener you pass it, `answers`.

Finish `prepare` and the two methods of `Answers`, marked `TODO`. A purchase waiting for its score must not hold up the others, each score must reach its own purchase, and a purchase the service can't score goes on without one. About eight lines in total.
The tests deploy a real TransactionManager with Q2, in the test's own JVM, and give it a single session. Their scorer holds some purchases until the test releases them, so several can wait at once.

cases.says: a purchase with a low score reaches the deciding participant with its score and is approved
a purchase with a high score reaches the deciding participant with its score and is declined
a purchase waiting for its score gives its session back, so the next purchase is answered meanwhile
the callback finds its own transaction through what it was handed, not through a field the next purchase overwrites
a callback without a score must still resume the transaction, or the purchase is never answered

origin.section: 4.7 `PAUSE` Gives the Session Back While You Wait

concepts: A participant that returns PAUSE frees its session; the callback finds its Context through handBack and always resumes, and a later participant decides.
